meta.title: Delhi new domestic water connection grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the new-connection application form was read but never filled in or submitted, and the application-status route was read but never queried with a reference number; the Delhi Jal Board citizens charter carries no visible issue date inside the document and its own text refers to a Board resolution of 26 October 2021 and to timelines extended to 30 September 2022, so parts of it predate the access date even though the hosting page displays a last-updated date of 3 September 2026; areas under the New Delhi Municipal Council and the Delhi Cantonment Board are outside the Board's route and outside this scoped row. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

agencies.name: Delhi Jal Board, Government of NCT of Delhi

scenarios.label: Delhi new domestic water connection
scenarios.summary: The individual owner of a built residential property with no connection applies to the city's water utility for a new domestic water supply, with sewer only where the same application covers it. Bulk or high-rise connections, commercial use, regularisation of unauthorised connections, name transfer on an existing account and tanker supply are excluded.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a resident of Delhi who owns the premises can apply for a new water connection.
claims.notes: A rule that decides who qualifies. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the owner limb, the tenant limb, the proof condition and the territorial exception.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a tenant of the premises may equally apply for a new water connection.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_who_can_apply. The tenant limb is separately checkable from the owner limb.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ requires the applicant to hold valid proof of identity together with proof of property ownership.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_who_can_apply. The proof condition is separately checkable from who may apply.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ excepts the areas under the control of NDMC and the Delhi Cantonment Board from the new-connection route.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_who_can_apply. The territorial exception tells the applicant where the route does not run and is separately checkable from the rule it excepts.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a new connection may be sanctioned only where the Board has provided or extended the water distribution system in the applicant's area.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the take-over limb of the same precondition is asserted separately by claim_delhi_water_network_precondition_2.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ extends that precondition to an area the Board has taken over for water supply and sewer maintenance.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_network_precondition, which carried two ways the network precondition can be met.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that there should be no accumulated arrears on account of water charges on the premises for which the connection has been applied.
The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that an application may be made once construction is completed.
claims.notes: Matches this scenario's trigger, an existing built residential property. The FAQ puts this limb on the owner or occupier, who are covered by claim_delhi_water_who_can_apply and claim_delhi_water_who_can_apply_2. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the completion rule, the authorisation condition and the vacant-plot exclusion.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ requires the completed construction to be authorised.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_completed_authorised_construction. The authorisation condition is separately checkable from the completion rule.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that no regular connection will be allowed on a vacant plot.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_completed_authorised_construction. The FAQ's wording is 'a vacant plot or piece of land'; both describe the same excluded case.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that only one water connection is sanctioned per dwelling unit.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the building-height rule is asserted separately by claim_delhi_water_one_connection_per_dwelling_2.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that individual connections may be sanctioned only for dwelling units within a building height of up to 15 metres.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_one_connection_per_dwelling. The height rule marks the boundary with the excluded high-rise and bulk routes.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the applicant should have a proof of identity document and a property ownership document as a condition for sanction of a new water connection.
The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter publishes a simplified document list for unauthorised or regularised colonies, urban or rural villages and slum katras.
claims.notes: An actionable document list for the colony categories named. It does not state the list for a property outside those categories, where the FAQ's identity-and-ownership condition applies instead. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the scope of the list and its three requirements.

claims.text: Under that list proof of identity of the present address may be a voter ID card, ration card, passport, PAN card, driving licence, Aadhaar card, bank passbook or a government photo identity card.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_simplified_document_list. This fragment carries the charter's published list of accepted identity proofs, which is one published list and is waived on the manifest entry.

claims.text: Under that list the applicant must also submit the last three months' paid electricity bills in the applicant's name.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_simplified_document_list. A separately checkable document requirement.

claims.text: Under that list an undertaking replaces ownership documents that are not available, where ownership is undisputed.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_simplified_document_list. A separately checkable document requirement.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board application form for a new connection requires a passport-size photograph of the applicant to be uploaded as an image file of less than 1 MB.
claims.notes: Observed on the current public form. The form was read only; nothing was uploaded.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ publishes a table of charges applicable to a new water and sewer connection for a domestic property.
claims.notes: Amounts a citizen pays, listed line by line for the domestic category, which is this scenario's category. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into one claim per charge line.

claims.text: That table gives an application fee for water of Rs. 10.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_domestic_charges_table; one charge line, one claim.

claims.text: That table gives an opening fee of Rs. 250 for water and Rs. 250 for sewer.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_domestic_charges_table; one charge line, one claim.

claims.text: That table gives a trade advance of Rs. 5,000.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_domestic_charges_table; one charge line, one claim.

claims.text: That table gives an occupier security of Rs. 500 for water and Rs. 500 for sewer.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_domestic_charges_table; one charge line, one claim.

claims.text: That table gives road restoration charges of Rs. 1,600 for water and Rs. 3,200 for sewer where the distance from the property to the DJB network is up to 5 metres.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_domestic_charges_table; one charge line, one claim. The distance condition is part of this line as published.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states a fixed development charge of Rs. 45,000 for water plus sewer in unauthorised regularised colonies where the plot size is up to 50 square metres.
claims.notes: A charge that turns on the colony's status, not on regularising an unauthorised connection, which this scenario excludes. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the two published amounts.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states the same development charge as Rs. 1,00,000 where the plot size is beyond 50 square metres.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_development_charges_unauthorised_colonies, which carried two amounts in one sentence.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the application form is available at every office of the Zonal Revenue Officer at a nominal fee of Rs. 10.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the counter availability and fee, what the fee covers, and the download route.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the Rs. 10 covers the cost of the form together with the processing fee.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_application_form_fee. What the fee covers is separately checkable from its amount.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the application form can also be downloaded from the consumer portal.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_application_form_fee. The download route is separately checkable from the counter route.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter states that doorstep delivery of the sanction of a new water connection is available through the toll-free number 1076.
claims.notes: The charter's wording covers a new water or sewer connection; this scenario is the water limb. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the availability of the service and its fee.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter states that a fee of Rs. 50 is charged for providing the doorstep service.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_doorstep_fee. The amount is separately checkable from the availability of the service.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter's table of services gives new water and sewer connection a delivery time of 15 days.
claims.notes: The same table gives 15 days for mutation, reopening and disconnection.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter states that doorstep delivery of public services has been implemented for sanction of a new water or sewer connection within a timeframe of 15 days.
The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the applicant must pay the demand raised by the ZRO office within fifteen days.
claims.notes: A deadline binding on the applicant after sanction, distinct from the Board's own delivery time. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the fifteen-day period, the alternative deadline and the consequence of missing it.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ gives the due date of the new connection bill as the alternative deadline for that payment.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_demand_payment_deadline. The alternative deadline is separately checkable from the fifteen-day period.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that the sanction is withdrawn where the demand is not paid by then.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_demand_payment_deadline. The consequence of missing the deadline is separately checkable from the deadline itself.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter names the Zonal Revenue Officer concerned as the officer responsible for a new water and sewer connection.
claims.notes: A designation tied to a jurisdiction rule: the officer is identified by the zone the property falls in.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a new connection will be sanctioned subject to the approval of the ZRO or competent authority.
claims.notes: Split by audit: the Executive Engineer half, which marks the boundary with the excluded commercial and bulk routes, is now carried by claim_delhi_water_executive_engineer_scope. What remains is the decision rule for the in-scope residential sanction, which is what the owner cell scores.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board publishes a contact directory that lists its designated JDR, DDR and Zonal Revenue Officer offices with office addresses and the assembly constituencies each office covers.
claims.notes: A specific office list a citizen can use to find the office holding their case. Named officers and their mobile numbers appear in the file and are deliberately not recorded here.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a new connection application can be submitted online on the consumer portal.
claims.notes: A step at submission, not after it; recorded for the route, not for the after-submission cell. Split by audit into the online route and the counter route, the latter carried by claim_delhi_water_application_submission_routes_2.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that a new connection application can also be submitted in the office of the concerned Zonal Revenue Office on all working days.
claims.notes: Split by audit from claim_delhi_water_application_submission_routes, with the source, grade, basis and status unchanged and the wording carried over from the same FAQ sentence. The counter route and its working-days condition are separately checkable from the online route. A step at submission, not after it; recorded for the route, not for the after-submission cell.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board portal publishes a Track Application Status route that takes an application reference number for a new connection.
claims.notes: The route's own field labels were observed; no reference number was entered, no login was used and no case data was retrieved. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the route, its public reachability and what it returns.

claims.text: That Track Application Status route is reachable without login.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_public_status_tracking_route. The route was observed without a login; no reference number was entered and no case data was retrieved.

claims.text: That route returns the applicant's details and the application status.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_public_status_tracking_route. Read from the route's own field labels; no reference number was entered and no case data was retrieved.

claims.text: That route returns a dated list of actions performed with remarks.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_public_status_tracking_route. Read from the route's own field labels; no reference number was entered and no case data was retrieved.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board citizens charter lists tracking of the status of an application among the 24x7 facilities of its customer portal, alongside submission of an application for a new water or sewer connection.
The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that only registered consumers can apply online for disconnection.
claims.notes: Boundary statement, recorded as a limitation and not used to support any positive cell value. The observation is the FAQ's own list. No login was used and no personal data was entered. Applying for a new connection is not in that list, which is why the new-connection form and the status route are reachable publicly. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the four surfaces the FAQ names and the inference drawn from them.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that only registered consumers can lodge a grievance online.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_registered_consumer_boundary. Boundary statement supporting no cell. No login was used and no personal data was entered.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that only registered consumers can update a profile online.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_registered_consumer_boundary. Boundary statement supporting no cell. No login was used and no personal data was entered.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that only registered consumers can view previous bills and receipts online.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_registered_consumer_boundary. Boundary statement supporting no cell. No login was used and no personal data was entered.

claims.text: Those registered-consumer surfaces sit past a boundary that this run did not cross.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_registered_consumer_boundary. This is the inference drawn from the FAQ's list. No login was used and no personal data was entered, so what lies past the boundary is unknown.

claims.text: What the applicant is shown at the moment a new connection is sanctioned is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related: the status route is public and was simply not queried, because entering a real application reference number is outside the safety boundary. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; whether a refusal states its reason is asserted separately.

claims.text: Whether a refusal of a new connection states its reason is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_delhi_water_sanction_outcome_notice_unknown. Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related: the status route is public and was simply not queried.

claims.text: The Delhi Jal Board FAQ states that assessment of technical feasibility and sanction of a commercial or bulk connection falls in the jurisdiction of the Executive Engineer concerned.
claims.notes: Split from claim_delhi_water_zro_approves_sanction by audit, with the source, grade and basis unchanged and the wording carried over verbatim. Retained under the primary scenario as route-selection evidence: it identifies the decision-maker for the commercial and bulk routes this scenario excludes, and so tells a scoped applicant that the ZRO route is theirs. Deliberately not cited by the owner cell, which scores the residential route.
